# Unlabel

> Unlabel is a free, open-source web tool that removes hidden metadata from photos before you post them to Instagram or anywhere else. It runs entirely in the browser: photos are never uploaded, there is no sign-up, and image quality is unchanged.

URL: https://anabansal.github.io/unlabel/
Source: https://github.com/anabansal/unlabel (MIT license)
Author: Anant Bansal

## What it removes
- Location: GPS coordinates, city and country fields (EXIF GPS, XMP, IPTC)
- Camera and phone: make, model, lens, serial number, maker notes
- Date and time the photo was taken, created or changed
- AI and source tags: C2PA Content Credentials (JPEG APP11, PNG caBX, WebP C2PA), IPTC DigitalSourceType values such as trainedAlgorithmicMedia and compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia, Stable Diffusion / ComfyUI prompts stored in PNG text chunks
- Edit history: XMP history, editing software, Photoshop/Lightroom settings, Samsung gallery-editor undo data
- Hidden preview thumbnails (EXIF IFD1, JFIF, Photoshop) that can reveal the uncropped photo
- Author, copyright, captions, keywords and comments
- Extra embedded data: HDR gain maps, depth maps, MPF images, data appended after the end of the image

## What it keeps
- Pixels: JPEG, PNG and WebP are edited at the byte level; the compressed image data is copied unchanged, so there is no re-compression or quality loss
- Colors: the ICC color profile (e.g. Display P3) and the Adobe color-transform marker are kept
- Orientation: a minimal EXIF block containing only the Orientation tag is written back, so photos do not rotate

## How to use
1. Open https://anabansal.github.io/unlabel/
2. Drag in one or more photos (or tap "choose photos", or paste). Cleaning starts automatically; there are no settings.
3. Each photo shows a card listing what was removed and a Download button. With several photos, "Download all" saves a ZIP.
4. Upload the cleaned copies to Instagram.

## Formats
- JPEG, PNG, WebP: cleaned losslessly
- HEIC, AVIF, GIF, TIFF and other formats the browser can decode: converted to a new JPEG (quality 0.95) with no metadata

## Limits
- It cannot remove invisible watermarks embedded in the pixels themselves (for example Google SynthID or other pixel-level watermarks).
- Platforms may still label content using other signals or the uploader's own disclosure.
